speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to pinpoint the cause, could you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have been affected, and for how long? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your vision, balance, or other neurological functions?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing that. The "drunken" appearance and clumsiness on the right side suggest a cerebellar or brainstem issue. Have you experienced any double vision, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your speech pattern? Also, when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very important detail. Given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, I am concerned about potential side effects on the central nervous system. Have you noticed any new weakness, numbness, or seizures recently? Also, do you have a specific date for your last dose of natalizumab?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of fever or recent infection makes a typical post-infectious presentation less likely, but your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use is highly concerning for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Have you noticed any changes in your sense of smell or taste? Also, do you have any facial drooping, difficulty speaking, or arm weakness on the right side?
